study type: Secondary analysis of a cohort study
outcome: Failed trial of labor after cesarean delivery (TOLAC)
Maternal morbidity (hysterectomy, transfusion, ICU transfer, venous thromboembolism, death)
Neonatal morbidity (5-minute Apgar score less than 5, cord pH less than 7.0, asphyxia, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy, neonatal death)
cohort: 6,033 women with term singleton gestations and a history of one prior cesarean delivery who attempted TOLAC
finding: Induction of labor in women with one prior cesarean delivery, compared with expectant management, is associated with an increased risk of failed TOLAC, increased risk of composite maternal morbidity at 39 weeks of gestation, and neonatal ICU admission at 37 weeks of gestation.
mod_finding: Induction of labor in women with one prior cesarean delivery, compared with expectant management, is associated with an increased risk of failed TOLAC.
gest_age: Term (37 weeks of gestation or greater)
